documentation: docs/MCU_MAPPING.md - section 4 defines this file (layer 3, the binding table), section 2 defines the MIDI numbers (layer 1), and section 2.7 records the hardware verification named below. Loaded and schema-validated by prism-surface in S22; a malformed profile falls back to the built-in defaults with a warning and never blocks startup.
notOurNoteMap: The note and CC numbers are deliberately NOT in this file. They live in exactly one place, prism_surface::profile::X_TOUCH, because a second copy of a 104-row table is a second thing to keep in step - which is what holding it in one constant was for. This file maps logical controls to commands.

measured.deviceReady: F0 00 00 66 14 01 <7 ascii serial> <4 ascii challenge> F7

untested.footSwitches: Notes 102 and 103 need a pedal in the FOOT SW jacks; nothing was plugged in. Neither note has an LED, which is expected of a jack.
untested.cablePull: Belongs to S21's connection handling rather than to the codec.

verification.knownFault: Saturating both directions at once - a burst of large SysEx writes while replies are outstanding - loses messages and can stop the surface transmitting entirely while it goes on receiving normally. Only a power cycle recovers it. Pace the outbound path (30 Hz, coalesced, minimum gap) and never poll the handshake. docs/MCU_MAPPING.md section 2.7.

sharedMode.summary: This surface is to be run in the X-Touch's combined Xctl+MC mode, driving the venue's sound console over Xctl and PrismDMX over MC at the same time. docs/MCU_MAPPING.md section 4.3.
sharedMode.provenance: Stated by the operator who owns and runs the desk. NOT measured in S20, which verified plain MC mode. Verifying it needs the sound console present.
sharedMode.consequence: Everything else - strips, faders, encoders, F-keys, bank and channel buttons - follows the operator's switch between the two hosts. Nothing is unreachable: SMPTE/Beats gives PrismDMX the whole surface at any time. What the permanent set buys is that it needs NO switch, which is what matters during a show.
sharedMode.designGoal: The transport section is the always-hot part of the console, so spend it on live-show work - free assignments included, such as a tap for speed against a particular speed master, a macro, or a look. It is explicitly NOT a requirement that everything important fit into five buttons. The bindings below are a reasonable starting point, not a layout.
sharedMode.feedbackRule: The shadow model may only drive LEDs for controls MC currently holds. Lighting a strip LED while the surface is showing the sound console is ignored at best, and fights that console's own feedback at worst.

reserved.reason: In the combined Xctl+MC mode this button switches the surface between the two hosts. It is the operator's way back to the sound desk, so PrismDMX never binds it - in ANY mode, so that one profile is safe on a desk whose mode nobody has checked. It also has no LED (measured, S20).
No LED on this device (measured, S20). Bindable in principle, but a control with no feedback is a poor place for an operating function, so the default profile leaves it alone.

bindingNotes: Each action's 't' is a prism_domain::Command variant. The arguments a command needs but a binding cannot know - executor_id, level, view_id - are supplied by layer 3 from the strip index, the current executor page (D7: executorPage * 8 + index) and the control's own value. 'Strip[*]' expands per strip.
openQuestionsForS22: SelectView in prism_domain takes an absolute view_id, but Channel left/right needs a relative move (D8). Either layer 3 resolves 'relative' against the session's view list, or the protocol grows a relative form. The 'relative' keys above are layer 3's, not the domain's.

SetExecutorMaster carries level: u16, and this surface reports 0..16380 in steps of 4 rather than 0..16383. Scale against verification.measured.faderMaxReported, or a fader against its end stop yields 99.98 per cent.
The Encoder Assign section has six buttons and docs/MCU_MAPPING.md section 4.1 names five feature groups. AssignInstrument is left unbound rather than doubled up.
Global.NameValue and Global.SmpteBeats are deliberately unbound - see 'reserved'. SmpteBeats must stay unbound and a loader should refuse a profile that binds it; NameValue is merely a bad idea.

The transport section and the jog wheel are the controls that reach PrismDMX without a mode switch (see sharedMode). Their function list should therefore grow the live-show entries an operator actually wants there - above all a tap for speed - rather than staying transport-shaped.

A tap for speed has no target yet. LearnSpeed exists only as an ExecutorButtonFunction, and speed masters are named in docs/DMX_MERGE.md section 4 item 3 with nothing implementing them and no domain type carrying one. S22 must not invent the command; the session that builds speed masters owes the type, the command and the function-list entry.

D7 (executor paging on Faderbank) and D8 (SelectView on Channel) sit outside the permanent set, so in shared operation they cost a switch to the full surface. Acceptable for setup-shaped work, and a reason not to put anything time-critical there.
